questions.question: The grid is made of identical parallelograms. With $\mathbf a=\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\mathbf c=\overrightarrow{CD}$, what is $\overrightarrow{EF}$?
questions.answer: **D.** From E to F is three steps in the direction of AB and one step opposite to CD.

questions.question: Four female and four male students sit around a circular table, alternating. In how many ways can this be done?
questions.answer: **B.** Seat one group in 3! ways, then the other in the 4 gaps in 4! ways.

A ball is kicked from $O$ with speed $V$ at angle $\alpha$: $\mathbf r=Vt\cos\alpha\,\mathbf i+\left(Vt\sin\alpha-\frac g2t^2\right)\mathbf j$. It reaches maximum height $h$ and lands on a hill at height $\frac h4$, a horizontal distance $d$ away. Show that $h=\dfrac{V^2\sin^2\alpha}{2g}$.

A ball is kicked from $O$ with speed $V$ at angle $\alpha$: $\mathbf r=Vt\cos\alpha\,\mathbf i+\left(Vt\sin\alpha-\frac g2t^2\right)\mathbf j$. It reaches maximum height $h$ and lands on a hill at height $\frac h4$, a horizontal distance $d$ away. Given $h=\frac{V^2\sin^2\alpha}{2g}$, show the time to land on the hill is $t=\dfrac{(2+\sqrt3)V\sin\alpha}{2g}$.
questions.answer:
$\frac g2t^2-Vt\sin\alpha+\dfrac{V^2\sin^2\alpha}{8g}=0$ gives $t=\dfrac{(2\pm\sqrt3)V\sin\alpha}{2g}$.

The ball is descending when it lands, so take the larger root.

Water has temperature $T=20+80e^{-0.2t}$ °C after $t$ minutes. How fast is it cooling when its temperature has fallen to half its initial value?
questions.answer: Initially $T=100$. $\dfrac{dT}{dt}=-0.2(T-20)$, so at $T=50$ it is cooling at $6$ °C/min.

questions.question: Part of $y=\sqrt{\cos3x\sin2x}$ is shown. By solving $\cos3x\sin2x=0$, show the smallest positive solution is $\dfrac\pi6$.
questions.answer: $\cos3x=0$ gives $x=\frac\pi6,\frac\pi2,\dots$; $\sin2x=0$ gives $x=0,\frac\pi2,\dots$. The smallest positive solution is $\frac\pi6$.

Sketch $y=-\tan^{-1}x$, labelling the point where $x=1$.
questions.answer: A decreasing curve through the origin with asymptotes $y=\pm\frac\pi2$, passing through $(1,-\frac\pi4)$.

$A$ lies on a circle with centre $O$, radius $a$. An arc with centre $A$ and radius $r<2a$ meets the circle at $B$ and $C$; arc $BC$ has length $\ell$ and $\angle BAC=2\theta$. Show that $r=2a\cos\theta$ and $\ell=4a\theta\cos\theta$.

$A$ lies on a circle with centre $O$, radius $a$. An arc with centre $A$ and radius $r<2a$ meets the circle at $B$ and $C$; arc $BC$ has length $\ell$ and $\angle BAC=2\theta$. Given $\ell=4a\theta\cos\theta$, show that $\ell$ is a maximum when $\theta=\cot\theta$.
questions.answer:
$\ell'=4a(\cos\theta-\theta\sin\theta)=0$ when $\theta=\cot\theta$.

$\ell''=-4a(2\sin\theta+\theta\cos\theta)<0$ for $0<\theta<\frac\pi2$, so it is a maximum.
